review_note: EO 853 'State of Emergency - Weather' was issued Nov 26, 2001, two days after the Nov 24, 2001 severe storms, tornadoes and flooding that FEMA declared as DR-1398; the index title names no hazard.

Associated Press via the Southeast Missourian, April 26, 2003: Gov. Ronnie Musgrove 'declared a state of emergency in three counties in the Jackson area' and one southern county after the storm. The story does not give the day it was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Jackson Free Press, April 7, 2008: Gov. Barbour declared a state of emergency at 2:45 p.m. that day for Hinds, Lauderdale, Leake, Madison, Neshoba, Newton, Scott, Smith, Rankin, Tippah, Warren and Yazoo counties, saying 'The amount of damage caused by the tornadoes and severe weather is devastating and widespread.'
Magnolia Tribune, August 29, 2008: 'Gov. Haley Barbour on Thursday declared a state of emergency for the southern region of the state' (Thursday, August 28) ahead of Hurricane Gustav.
Jackson Free Press, March 26, 2009: 'Governor Haley Barbour declared a State of Emergency today for the severe weather system' that struck late on March 25 and into March 26.

Associated Press via the Southeast Missourian, February 11, 2013: after Sunday's tornado in Hattiesburg, 'Gov. Phil Bryant declared a state of emergency.' The story does not give the day it was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

Associated Press via the Christian Science Monitor, December 24, 2014: 'Mississippi Gov. Phil Bryant declared an emergency for two southeastern counties' after the December 23 tornadoes. The story does not give the day it was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

International Business Times, December 24, 2015: 'Mississippi Governor Phil Bryant declared a state of emergency in the areas affected by the storms', after 14 tornadoes on December 23. The story does not give the day it was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
WREG, March 10, 2016: 'MS Governor Phil Bryant declares state of emergency' as heavy rain flooded the state.

WCBI, January 2, 2019: 'Mississippi Gov. Phil Bryant has issued a state of emergency declaration for eight counties' (Clarke, Covington, Forrest, Jasper, Jones, Lauderdale, Perry and Wayne), announced Tuesday night, January 1, for the December 27 storms.
WLBT, February 25, 2019: 'Governor Bryant declares State of Emergency in response to deadly storms', after the February 23 storms and the Columbus tornado.
WCBI, April 14, 2019: 'Governor Phil Bryant has declared a State of Emergency following widespread severe weather on Saturday' (April 13).
WLBT, May 12, 2019: Gov. Bryant said, 'This morning I signed a State of Emergency Declaration for all the affected areas of recent storms.'

WDAM, April 12, 2020: 'Gov. Reeves declares state of emergency after killer Easter storms.' MEMA's April 16 damage report adds that 'Governor Tate Reeves signed a State of Emergency in response to this severe weather outbreak.'
MEMA, October 7, 2020: 'Governor Tate Reeves issues a State of Emergency in anticipation of Hurricane Delta.'
MEMA, October 28, 2020: 'Governor Reeves has also signed a State of Emergency in anticipation of the storm.' The story does not give the day it was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.

MEMA, February 14, 2021: 'In consultation with Governor Reeves, Lieutenant Governor Delbert Hosemann signed the Proclamation for a State of Emergency, Sunday February 14, 2021' in anticipation of the winter storm.

MEMA, March 15, 2025: 'Governor Tate Reeves has issued a State of Emergency in all counties affected by the severe storms that occurred across Mississippi on March 14 and March 15, 2025.' SuperTalk Mississippi reported it was signed Saturday night, March 15.

WLOX, June 19, 2026: Gov. Reeves said, 'I have declared a State of Emergency in areas of Mississippi affected or potentially affected by these storms.' The story does not give the day it was signed, so the row carries the date of the report.
